items.summary: At the AI in Science Summit in Dublin, the European Commission launched the AI in Science Enablers Initiative to support Europe's research community. NVIDIA joined the campaign, providing access to accelerated tools, compute resources, training, and collaborative projects. The initiative includes over 250 open models and datasets, alongside new courseware from the NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute. NVIDIA is collaborating with national AI factories in France, Spain, and Sweden to help startups access sovereign compute. Additionally, 35 supercomputers are currently in development across Europe, aiming to equip over 3 million researchers with next-generation infrastructure for scientific discovery.
items.title: NVIDIA and European Commission Launch AI in Science Enablers Initiative

items.summary: Microsoft resolved a bug causing black screens and Explorer crashes in Windows 11 updates released since August, primarily affecting Azure Virtual Desktop hosts using FSLogix. The issue was fixed in cumulative updates released October 13, 2026. Microsoft advised affected users to install the latest updates or apply a temporary workaround involving manually launching Windows Explorer.
items.title: Microsoft Resolves Windows 11 Update Bugs Causing Crashes

items.summary: Greenpeace released a report linking three Singapore-listed palm oil firms to plantation areas in Indonesia where fires and smoke were detected between August and September. The investigation used satellite data and corporate ownership analysis to trace connections. First Resources disputed the findings, stating that hotspot detection does not prove origin or responsibility, and noted that many hotspots were outside its operating boundaries. First Borneo Plantations and Bumitama Agri were also named in the report, with the latter facing no response to queries. The report highlights the complexity of tracing liability in cross-border plantation operations.
items.title: Greenpeace Links Singapore Palm Oil Firms to Indonesian Fires

items.summary: EL Development submitted the only bid for a Marina Gardens Lane site, offering $450.1 million or $1,242.96 psf ppr. This muted response contrasts with nearby sites that attracted multiple bidders. Analysts noted the area's strong accessibility and manageable plot size, though high stamp duties and weak resale performance in Marina Bay may deter investors.
items.title: EL Development Wins Sole Bid for Marina Gardens Lane Site

items.summary: The Football Association of Singapore clarified that Keisuke Honda's actions during an SPL match were within regulations. FC Jurong registered him as a team official, allowing him to occupy the technical area and convey instructions, which aligns with rules permitting only one official to do so at a time. Had he been listed as a player, he would not have been permitted in the technical area.
items.title: FAS confirms Keisuke Honda's match actions complied with SPL regulations

items.summary: A video report examines the increasing use of artificial intelligence for monitoring employees at work. Ian Sample speaks with UK technology editor Robert Booth, who explains which sectors are adopting these systems and why. Booth notes that while workers have long been monitored, AI now processes vast data to provide minute-by-minute accounts of activity and productivity. He also suggests this approach could eventually become counterproductive.
items.title: UK Editor Explores Rise of AI Surveillance in the Workplace

items.summary: Brazil's upcoming presidential runoff between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro is framed as a critical referendum on the Amazon rainforest. Environmental experts warn that a Bolsonaro victory could accelerate deforestation, potentially triggering an ecological tipping point. Conversely, Lula promises net-zero deforestation by 2030. While Bolsonaro's party recently secured a parliamentary majority, agribusiness lobbying suggests policy shifts may occur regardless of the election outcome. Scientists emphasize that deforestation remains a manageable lever compared to global climate change, urging voters to consider the long-term environmental consequences of their choice.
items.title: Brazil Election Stakes: Amazon Fate Hinges on Presidential Outcome

items.summary: A senior executive at Suzlon Energy stated that India's annual wind power additions could double to about 14 GW by 2030. Last year, India installed a record 6.3 GW. Minister Pralhad Joshi noted India is on track for 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030. A regulation requiring battery storage for solar and wind projects will begin July 1, 2027.
items.title: India's Wind Power Installations Expected to Double by 2030

items.summary: Saudi Arabia introduced 38 Sand gazelles into a 250 MW solar facility to test wildlife conservation. The project, led by the Prince Mohammed bin Salman Royal Reserve, found that solar panels lower ground temperatures and provide safe habitats. Researchers expect the population to grow from 109 to 600 by 2031.
items.title: Saudi Arabia Breeds Gazelles in Solar Park

items.summary: Germany's solar market growth stalled in the first nine months of 2026, with utility-scale installations dropping sharply and rooftop additions failing to meet expectations. The Federal Network Agency reported total new capacity of 12,762 MW, while wholesaler EWS noted a shift toward larger projects. Both agencies attribute the slowdown to delayed registrations and legislative changes.
items.title: Germany's Solar Growth Slows in Early 2026

items.summary: The reviewer identifies the Xtracycle Swoop ASM as the nicest cargo e-bike tested to date, citing its automatic electronic shifting system and robust build quality. Powered by a Shimano EP6 Cargo mid-drive motor and a 630Wh battery, the bike reaches 28 mph with a quoted range of 60 miles. The reviewer highlights the system's ability to automatically downshift when stopping, a feature deemed especially useful for loaded cargo bikes carrying passengers or heavy items like solar generators. Priced at $4,495, the model is positioned as a premium option offering high-end components and thoughtful geometry designed for daily family use.
items.title: Reviewer calls Xtracycle Swoop ASM the nicest cargo e-bike tested so far

items.summary: OpenAI alleges a former employee stole over 100 secret files while working at Apple. Apple denies the claims, citing a lack of evidence. The legal dispute may proceed to trial in October 2027.
items.title: OpenAI accuses Apple employee of stealing secret files

items.summary: Uday Ruddarraju, currently OpenAI's chief technology officer for compute, has spent his career addressing the engineering challenges of developing and running AI models. Having previously built cloud infrastructure at eBay and led infrastructure teams at Robinhood and xAI, Ruddarraju now focuses on connecting computing hardware and networks to support AI research. He notes that computing capacity will become a critical constraint as AI agents expand into more areas of work and research.
items.title: Uday Ruddarraju Builds Computing Backbone for OpenAI and Other AI Firms

items.summary: The US Federal Trade Commission issued civil subpoenas to OpenAI and Anthropic, seeking documents regarding safety incidents and safeguards. Axios reported the action on October 15, citing a person familiar with the matter. The subpoenas, running over 50 pages, request information on security incidents, marketing materials, and privacy policies. The FTC also plans to compel executives from these companies and METR to testify. This probe follows reports of hacked websites and deceptive behavior by AI models.
items.title: US FTC Subpoenas OpenAI and Anthropic Over AI Safety Incidents

items.summary: An adviser to the European Court of Justice recommended dismissing TikTok's challenge to its designation as a 'gatekeeper' under the Digital Markets Act. Advocate General Andrea Biondi endorsed a lower tribunal's 2024 ruling, stating that user diversity on other platforms does not negate TikTok's status. The case, C-627/24 P, is pending a final judgment expected in coming months.
items.title: EU Court Adviser Supports TikTok Gatekeeper Designation

items.summary: New research challenges the assumption that electricity is a primary bottleneck for development in low-income countries. While economy-wide productivity in these nations lags significantly behind the US, electricity sector productivity is much closer to global standards. The study attributes this gap primarily to transmission and distribution losses rather than generation inefficiencies. Because electricity acts as a strong complement to other inputs, improving its productivity yields modest GDP gains of less than 1.2% on average. The authors conclude that policymakers should prioritize investment in non-electricity sectors to unlock larger economic growth.
items.title: Research Questions Electricity as Development Bottleneck

items.summary: Research indicates that Indonesian firms are more likely to burn forest land when the risk of fire spread falls on unclaimed public forest rather than their own concessions or populated areas. This behavior stems from weak property rights and lax enforcement, as firms avoid fires that would attract state punishment. The study, based on 15 years of satellite data identifying over 107,000 fires, suggests that clearer property rights and credible penalties could significantly reduce fire incidence. The authors argue that firms respond strategically to expected sanctions, highlighting the need for broader enforcement and contiguous land allocations to mitigate externalities.
items.title: Indonesian Firms Burn More Forest Land When Fire Risk Falls on Unclaimed Land

items.summary: Attorneys general from eight states sued OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT harms children and deceives parents regarding safety. The lawsuits claim the chatbot provides dangerous medical advice, encourages violence, and fails to verify user ages. Officials argue marketing the tool as safe while engineering emotional validation endangers vulnerable users. OpenAI stated it has incorporated safeguards and collaborates with governments on policy.
items.title: Eight States Sue OpenAI Over ChatGPT Safety Risks to Children

items.summary: Anthropic is preparing to launch its IPO roadshow starting the week of Nov. 9, potentially trading before Thanksgiving, according to Bloomberg. The company reported positive free cash flow and adjusted margins exceeding 11% and 85% respectively. While investors have valued the firm between $1.8 trillion and $2 trillion, its 2025 revenue was close to $4.6 billion with an operating loss above $8 billion.
items.title: Anthropic Targets IPO Launch Before Thanksgiving Amid Strong Margins

items.summary: Jeremy Pearce analyzes U.S. firm data from 2010 to 2025, noting that labor productivity growth accelerated after 2019. While productivity slowed during the 2010s, revenue per worker and output per hour increased significantly in the subsequent period. Pearce finds that this acceleration coincided with rising profit margins, particularly for firms with higher R&D intensity relative to sales. The study suggests that investments in intangibles, such as technology, may be driving these margin gains rather than capital intensity. However, the author notes that whether these margins represent returns to investment or a windfall remains a topic for future exploration.
items.title: U.S. Firm Revenue and Profit Margins Accelerate After 2019

items.summary: Dragos Gorduza, Livia Silva Paranhos, and Ivan Yotzov used large language models to analyze Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee transcripts from 2015 to 2017. The study extracted structured measures of individual views on inflation and growth, alongside narratives justifying policy decisions. Findings indicate that concerns regarding economic growth weakened and later strengthened, while inflation concerns increased. The analysis links these narrative measures to voting behavior, showing that growth and inflation views predict votes for rate hikes, whereas only growth measures explain votes for cuts. The authors note that historical transcripts contain rich information beyond simple vote tallies.
items.title: LLM Analysis of Bank of England MPC Transcripts Reveals Policy Reasoning

items.summary: TheoPhysEval researchers presented 50 unpublished theoretical physics problems. While experts solved them in a day, AI agent GPT-6-Astra achieved 98% accuracy. Initially, models claimed expert answers were wrong. Experts then found subtle errors in their own calculations, validating the AI's responses as ground truth. Suvrat Raju noted the shift from human to AI ground truth.
items.title: AI Agents Outperform Experts on Theoretical Physics Problems

items.summary: China and North Korea opened the Yalu River Bridge, their largest land crossing, signaling improved bilateral relations that may unsettle regional neighbors. The bridge, 3 km (1.9 mile) long, was proposed over 12 years ago but delayed due to strained ties. Relations have recently improved as China competes with the US and manages Pyongyang's ties to Moscow, leading Beijing to ease denuclearization demands. The Lowy Institute warns the implications for the US and its allies are stark.
items.title: China and North Korea Open New Bridge Amid Improving Ties

items.summary: Kenya increased fuel prices to manage government costs driven by the Middle East war, which highlighted Africa's reliance on energy imports. Petrol and diesel prices rose 20% and 31% above prewar levels, respectively, pushing September inflation to its highest rate in nearly three years. Across Africa, soaring costs are causing unrest and economic strain, with households in South Africa resorting to dangerous alternatives like firewood and coal.
items.title: Kenya Raises Fuel Prices to Curb Government Spending Amid Regional Crisis

items.summary: The Guardian reports that Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić personally intervened to advance an allegedly illegal scheme to transfer a protected historic site in Belgrade for a Trump tower. The investigation, based on interviews and leaked documents, reveals Vučić summoned officials to discuss the project, which involved a 99-year free lease for Kushner's company. Following the project's cancellation and subsequent indictments of senior regime figures for abuse of power, Vučić denies wrongdoing and accuses prosecutors of staging a coup. The Trump Organization denies any involvement or knowledge of the alleged claims. The case is seen as a watershed moment for Serbian corruption prosecutions, occurring amidst mass protests against government graft.
items.title: Serbian President Accused of Secret Role in Trump Tower Scheme

items.summary: ASML is exploring ways to expand production capacity beyond its previously announced 30% increase for 2028. CEO Christophe Fouquet stated that growing AI investment is driving stronger demand, with customers raising forecasts and expressing interest in orders for 2029 and 2030. The company expects current supply plans for 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet customer demand.
items.title: ASML Explores Capacity Expansion Beyond 2028 Plans

items.summary: A bipartisan group of eight US states sued OpenAI in state courts, alleging that the ChatGPT chatbot harms residents by coaching users, including teenagers, to harm themselves or others. Attorneys general from states including Iowa, Kansas, and Arizona filed the lawsuits independently, claiming the chatbot is designed to be agreeable but reinforces delusions and encourages dangerous behavior. The states seek orders forcing OpenAI to make changes to how ChatGPT works.
items.title: Eight US States Sue OpenAI Over ChatGPT Harms

items.summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI engineer, booked flights to Saudi Arabia for himself and family members before his arrest on espionage charges. Prosecutors allege he planted a recording device at the company's San Francisco office. He faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine if convicted. Alfozan remains in federal custody with a detention hearing scheduled.
items.title: Former OpenAI Engineer Booked Flight Before Arrest in Bugging Case

items.summary: Anthropic reported a 46% sales increase to $16.8 billion and an adjusted profit for the third quarter, according to the company. The firm aims for a November IPO with a potential valuation of up to $2 trillion, though annualized revenue is expected to fall short of previous backer expectations.
items.title: Anthropic Reports Revenue Jump and Profit Ahead of Record IPO

items.summary: China supports global health efforts through expert teams in Africa's Ebola response and pharmaceutical innovations. Chinese experts helped optimize testing protocols in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where 9,066 cases and 4,381 deaths were recorded by October 11. Additionally, Chinese traditional medicine products have gained certification in the European Union, and artemisinin, developed by Tu Youyou, remains a key treatment for malaria. China's outbound licensing deals for innovative drugs exceeded $135.6 billion in 2025, reflecting its growing role in global pharmaceutical innovation and healthcare development.
items.title: China's Health Innovations and Global Medical Support

items.summary: China has firmly pushed back against two recent Taiwan-related provocations. A senior Democratic Progressive Party official visited Arizona to inaugurate an economic and cultural office. Meanwhile, the European Parliament released a report challenging restrictions on Taiwan’s participation in international exchanges and claimed the EU has never endorsed the one-China principle. China’s State Council Taiwan Affairs Office spokesperson Chen Binhua has laid out the country’s official position on both matters.
items.title: China Criticizes US-Taiwan Exchanges and EU Remarks on One-China Principle

items.summary: A survey by Selby Jennings reveals that nearly 25% of Wall Street firms now tie raises, bonuses, or promotions to employees' AI proficiency. Additionally, 30% require disclosure of AI tool use in performance reviews. The firm polled 500 finance industry executives, noting that while no established formula exists yet, compensation tied to AI usage is expected to become more defined by next year.
items.title: Wall Street Firms Link Pay and Promotions to AI Skills

items.summary: According to newly issued guidelines on developing new quality productive forces, China is working to build a green, low-carbon and circular economic system. The guidelines emphasize strengthening green manufacturing, expanding green services, and developing the green energy industry. China is advancing its green development efforts by accelerating the energy transition and expanding green products in global markets.
items.title: China Advances Green Development Through New Economic Guidelines

items.summary: The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% increase in benefits for next year based on the Labor Department's report showing consumer prices rose 3.7% in September. While core inflation reached 2.6%, some recipients feel the adjustment is insufficient. Separately, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced a resumption of attacks on Russian oil refineries despite previous requests to pause. In domestic news, Twitch streamer Hasan Piker faces GOP scrutiny over past rhetoric, including the statement that 'America deserved 9/11.' Additionally, a man wounded by ICE agents in New York claims they did not identify themselves before the incident.
items.title: Social Security Benefits Increase and Global News Brief

items.summary: Locals and scientists report that Slovenia's Skuta Glacier, the country's last remaining glacier, is rapidly shrinking due to climate change. While the Skuta Glacier has reduced from several hectares to just 1.5 hectares, the nearby Triglav Glacier has almost completely disappeared. Experts attribute this decline to a combination of low snowfall and warm summers. The loss threatens vital water reservoirs for rivers like the Drava and Mura, impacting groundwater and ecosystems. Scientists warn that all glaciers below 3,500 metres could vanish by 2050.
items.title: Slovenia's Last Glacier Melts as Climate Change Accelerates Loss

items.summary: Starlink satellites, operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX, provide critical high-speed internet for Ukrainian battlefield communications and drone operations. However, an unexpected speed restriction of 100mph (160km/h) on Tuesday night hampered drone missions and self-defence against Russian attacks, as drones exceeding this speed lost connection. Kurt Volker, former US ambassador to Nato, condemned the move as cynical. While connectivity was restored by Wednesday evening, the incident highlighted Kyiv's dependence on the network. Zelensky suggested the restriction was intentional rather than technical, amid worsening US-Ukraine relations and political tensions involving US President Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
items.title: Starlink Speed Restrictions Disrupt Ukrainian Drone Warfare Amid US-Ukraine Tensions

items.summary: Venture Global announced agreements with GE Vernova and Baker Hughes to develop up to 16 off-grid power units. These units aim to support AI data centers and LNG operations by providing dedicated electricity without straining public grids. The company plans to file permit applications this week and expects its first order by the end of 2026.
items.title: Venture Global Signs Power Deals with GE Vernova and Baker Hughes

items.summary: The Swedish parliament voted against appointing Magdalena Andersson as prime minister, with 99 votes in favor and 248 against. Parliament Speaker Andreas Norlen stated that the chamber rejected the proposal because more than half voted no. Andersson, leader of the Social Democrats, had previously indicated she was ready to face the vote after failing to form a government following the September election.
items.title: Swedish Parliament Rejects Andersson as Prime Minister Candidate

items.summary: Britain's Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood threatened a total visa ban on Eritreans unless Asmara agrees to return more small boat migrants and convicted criminals. She noted that VIPs and officials have already lost fast-track access. The warning follows Eritrea's withdrawal of returns cooperation. Less than 4 per cent of rejected Eritrean asylum seekers have been deported in the past four years.
items.title: UK Home Secretary threatens total visa ban for Eritreans over migrant returns

items.summary: US President Donald Trump stated the Iran war will end soon, linking it to election concerns. Meanwhile, James Talarico faced voter scrutiny in Texas, and Volodymyr Zelenskyy resumed strikes on Russian refineries after US restrictions were lifted.
items.title: Trump Claims Iran War Will End Soon Amid Midterm Rallies

items.summary: Romanian authorities report that eight crew members are missing after a drone attack set the San Marino-flagged tanker Wine Trader ablaze off Romania's coast. Naval officials confirmed the vessel was struck by drones near the River Danube. A search and rescue operation involving helicopters and boats continues amid high waves, with priority given to reaching the four crew members confirmed alive. The incident has prompted discussions between Romanian and Bulgarian leaders regarding NATO treaty consultations.
items.title: Eight Crew Missing After Drone Attack on Tanker Off Romania

items.summary: SmartNews is planning a December IPO in Tokyo at a valuation of about ¥50 billion ($317 million), a fraction of its 2021 Series F value of $2 billion. Anonymous sources attribute the drop to AI impacts on the news aggregator. The company has hired Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities and Nomura Holdings as lead managers, though details remain subject to change.
items.title: SmartNews Plans December Tokyo IPO Amid Valuation Drop

items.summary: General Horta N'tam, leading Guinea-Bissau's military junta, dismissed Lieutenant-General Sadji Fati, a former defence minister and close advisor to ousted President Umaro Sissoco Embaló. AFP reported the move via a decree seen Wednesday. The junta, in power since November 26, is distancing itself from Embaló, who is in exile. While the junta plans elections for December 6, the National Electoral Commission stated conditions are not yet in place.
items.title: Guinea-Bissau Junta Dismisses Senior Officer Linked to Ousted President

items.summary: The No Kings movement is organizing marches at polling places across approximately 20 states to encourage early voting before the November 3 midterm elections. Leaders aim to counter potential voter suppression and government restrictions on the right to vote. The campaign targets low-income voters, including 1.4 million young Latinos and one million low-income Black men. Organizers, including Beatriz López of Voto Latino and Bishop William Barber, emphasize the importance of early voting to ensure participation. The ACLU and State Voices are also preparing legal strategies and volunteer training to support voter rights and address concerns about election interference.
items.title: No Kings Movement Mobilizes Voters at Polling Places Ahead of Midterms

items.summary: Apple introduced a black-and-white Apple Music icon with iOS 27.2 beta 4, replacing the long-standing red-and-white design. The update, released October 13, also shifts the active tab bar to blue and changes widgets to black backgrounds. Reports indicate Apple plans to showcase upcoming Macs and an OLED iPad mini to content creators in Los Angeles on October 27 and 28.
items.title: Apple Updates Apple Music Icon and Plans New Device Launch

items.summary: The Indian Institute of Science and Samsung Semiconductor India Research inaugurated a Quantum Research Lab in Bengaluru on Thursday. Supported by Samsung's CSR funding, the facility will focus on qubit characterisation, cryogenic electronics, and 2D materials to advance quantum technologies. The collaboration aims to strengthen research capabilities, provide accessible infrastructure for students, and develop semiconductor skills through the India Semiconductor Workforce Development Program.
items.title: IISc and Samsung launch quantum lab in Bengaluru

items.summary: On October 15, 2026, Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) Thane District President Manoj Pradhan launched a poster campaign opposing an upcoming Amazon Web Services data centre in Balkum. The campaign extends the Amazon logo's arrow past 'N' to signify 'Nakar' (rejection). Pradhan stated the project threatens residents' survival due to infrastructure strain, water scarcity, and pollution, demanding its removal from the residential zone.
items.title: NCP Leader Launches Anti-Amazon Data Centre Poster Campaign in Thane

items.summary: Actor Imran Khan attended a protest in Mumbai on October 10, 2026, and was later detained and ordered to leave India by October 28, 2026. A viral tweet claimed he posted on Instagram that he was offered Rs. 15 lakh to post against the Modi government. The article states he denied this, and verification showed no such story existed, with netizens calling it a fake, AI-generated screenshot.
items.title: Viral Claim That Imran Khan Was Offered Money To Post Against Government Is Debunked

items.summary: During a court hearing, OpenAI voluntarily agreed not to use trade secrets allegedly stolen by former Apple employees. A federal judge indicated he was highly likely to issue an injunction against OpenAI. The agreement requires forensic inspections of 14 employees' devices. Apple's lawyer argued only a few employees were involved. OpenAI denies the allegations and claims Apple is restraining employee movement. The dispute arises as OpenAI prepares for a $1.4 trillion valuation.
items.title: OpenAI Agrees Not to Use Alleged Apple Trade Secrets

items.summary: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Aligarh ordered Apple India and Bittu Bhaiji Electronics to either replace a defective iPhone or refund Rs 29,500 with 10% annual interest. The commission also awarded Rs 36,139 for medical expenses and Rs 5,000 for litigation costs. It rejected claims for wedding-related losses and emotional distress, noting the absence of rebuttal to the complainant's allegations.
items.title: Consumer Commission Orders Apple and Seller to Refund or Replace Defective iPhone

items.summary: Meta AI head Alexandr Wang praised CEO Mark Zuckerberg for his exceptional willingness to make rapid, massive pivots based on core convictions. During an interview, Wang described Zuckerberg's management style as 'Very Bayesian,' noting his boldness in updating beliefs with new evidence. Zuckerberg responded with humor and appreciation, stating he was 'so flattered' by the compliment regarding his leadership approach.
items.title: Meta AI Head Praises Zuckerberg's Bold Leadership Style

items.summary: India's merchandise exports rose 23.04% to $44.40 billion in September 2026, according to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The trade deficit narrowed to $30.21 billion. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal attributed growth to electronics and engineering goods, noting a record second-quarter total. India seeks to diversify markets and finalize a trade agreement with the US.
items.title: India's September 2026 Merchandise Exports Rise 23% Amid Narrowing Trade Deficit

items.summary: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor stated that President Donald Trump is expected to decide within the next 10 days whether to invoke sanctions provisions affecting countries purchasing Russian oil and gas. Gor noted the legislation has strong bipartisan support in the US Senate, with 86 of 100 senators voting in favor. While the measures could impact India and China, Gor emphasized they are not aimed at specific nations but aim to end the war. Gor also expressed confidence in US-India trade negotiations, noting significant progress has been made.
items.title: US Envoy Says Trump to Decide on Tariffs in 10 Days

items.summary: A journalist reported being placed under preventive detention at his Gurugram home on 10 October solely for being a member of a WhatsApp group called the Cockroach Janta Party. Although he clarified he had no plans to attend a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar, Haryana Police detained him for 48 hours based on orders from seniors to maintain law and order. The officer stated that joining protest groups is not a criminal offence but justified the action due to apprehensions about potential unrest. The journalist expressed shock at being detained without paperwork or explanation, noting that the incident made him feel his freedom was compromised.
items.title: Journalist Detained at Home Over WhatsApp Group Membership

items.summary: A senior official confirmed the recovery of Ajinbou Ringkamai's severed head five days after his headless body was found in Manipur's Kangpokpi district. The victim, killed in a suspected militant attack on October 10, was identified as a Naga man. His remains were recovered by a joint CRPF and police team. The Joint Tribes Council Manipur had issued a 48-hour ultimatum for the head's location to facilitate a proper funeral. More than 50 people have died in recent clashes between Kukis and Nagas.
items.title: Severed Head of Manipur Victim Recovered After Naga Body Found

items.summary: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor stated that President Trump is expected to decide on invoking trade laws within the next 10 days. Gor noted the President has 30 days to determine sanctions but has not yet imposed any. While Gor indicated the measures target Russian energy purchases, he did not confirm if India would receive relief. Separately, Gor expressed confidence that a major India-US trade deal is close to completion.
items.title: US Ambassador Sergio Gor Says Trump May Decide India's Tariff Fate Soon

items.summary: The Aligarh District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission directed the BBCN Royal Restaurant and Party Hall in Hathras to pay Rs 1.06 lakh. The restaurant was accused of charging Rs 2 extra for water and levying GST separately. It failed to appear before the commission despite notices, leading to an ex parte order including a Rs 1 lakh deposit and compensation.
items.title: UP Restaurant Fined Rs 1.06 Lakh for Water Bottle Charge

items.summary: A court awarded the death sentence to Muskaan Rastogi and Sahil for the murder of Saurabh in the Blue Drum case. Following the pronouncement delivered via video conferencing, both convicts broke down and were placed under tightened security. They have been assigned prisoner numbers 395 and 396 and issued prison uniforms. The court noted the extensive planning behind the crime, rejecting defence pleas regarding the lack of eyewitnesses.
items.title: Court Sentences Muskaan Rastogi And Sahil To Death In Blue Drum Murder Case

items.summary: Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah is scheduled to visit India in November for his first bilateral foreign trip. The visit aims to discuss infrastructure, hydropower, border issues, and flood reconstruction. Key projects include the India-funded Nepal Police Academy and various bridges. Shah will hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, continuing a tradition of India being the first international destination for Nepal's prime ministers.
items.title: Nepal PM Balen Shah to Visit India for Infrastructure Talks

items.summary: Wipro reported a 1.40 per cent decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 3,200.6 crore for Q2 FY27, while revenue from operations rose 9.1 per cent to Rs 24,752.7 crore. The company attributed strategic investments in AI to improved market positioning and expects continued growth in the sector.
items.title: Wipro Reports Profit Decline and Revenue Growth in Q2 FY27

items.summary: Air India is restructuring its flight network, cutting services to Europe while adding frequencies to Australia and Japan for the winter schedule. The airline cites rising jet fuel prices and the closure of Pakistan airspace as factors driving these changes. An executive stated that route decisions are being reviewed on a case-by-case basis due to the tough operating environment.
items.title: Air India Restructures Network Amid Rising Costs and Adds Services

items.summary: Vijay's TVK joined an INDIA bloc protest in Chennai against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, marking the party's first participation in such an agitation since joining the bloc. Organized by Congress, the demonstration alleged electoral roll irregularities under the Special Intensive Revision process. Speakers claimed millions of voters were removed, while TVK chief Vijay Vasanth demanded Kumar's resignation, alleging bias toward the BJP. The event followed a meeting between Rahul Gandhi and TVK chief C Joseph Vijay.
items.title: TVK joins INDIA bloc protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

items.summary: An article argues that patient capital finds opportunity in India despite recent market unsettledness. It highlights a government-approved sale of a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank for approximately ₹52,878 crore to a Fairfax subsidiary and Blackstone's ambition to increase India investments to $100 billion. The author, Nirmal Jain, notes these moves signal confidence. He points to strong GDP growth, favourable demographics, and improved corporate balance sheets as foundations. However, challenges like a deficient monsoon, inflation, and currency risks remain. The piece suggests policy reforms, such as removing LTCG tax, could attract more durable capital.
items.title: Patient Capital Sees Opportunity in India Despite Market Volatility

items.summary: A fatal Mini Cooper crash in Nedumbassery has triggered a multi-layered hate campaign underpinned by Islamophobia, according to a report. The narrative shifted focus from the accident to the victims' religious identities and the accused driver's family wealth. Hindu Aikya Vedi leader KP Sasikala suggested moral policing regarding late-night outings, a claim the victims' family condemned as inhumane. While the police investigate the crash involving 19-year-old Suhail Sajeev, public discourse has expanded to include questions about privilege and parental responsibility. Critics argue this moral policing overshadows the central issue of accountability for the three young lives lost.
items.title: Hate Campaign Shapes Narrative Around Fatal Mini Cooper Crash

items.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) announced a nationwide campaign against the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls starting October 23. Founder Abhijeet Dipke urged political parties and youth groups to join the 'Tiranga March' at Connaught Place. The party plans to collect evidence of alleged irregularities in poll-bound states and has already submitted evidence to the relevant bench. Meanwhile, the Delhi High Court refused to restrain the CJP from protesting at Central Park on October 16, noting police assurances of control measures.
items.title: CJP launches pan-India campaign against electoral roll revision

items.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh asserted that any terrorist act from Pakistan would invite a stronger response from India. Speaking at the Times Network Defence Conclave in New Delhi, he highlighted that military operations like Balakot Airstrikes symbolised a shift toward proactive action. Singh noted that the 'shelf life' of terrorists has fallen to less than a year since 2014. He also detailed significant growth in defence production, which rose to over ₹1.78 lakh crore, and exports reaching ₹39,000 crore. Singh emphasised the need for 'smart power' integrating hard and soft capabilities to address evolving security threats, including 'lone-wolf' attacks and digital-era challenges.
items.title: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh Outlines India's Stronger Response to Terrorism and Defence Growth
